samples.question: The sandy board is scattered with small decorative coloured squares, and exactly three pale ROSTER panels sit on it, each in a different far corner of the board. Only what is drawn inside the three rosters decides the answer; every square lying on the bare board is decoration and means nothing. Each roster carries six large square TOKENS, and each roster carries exactly one token of every colour: red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple. Inside every token sit between one and four small dark square PIPS, and that number is the token's pip count. The tokens are arranged in a different order inside each roster, so a token's position tells you nothing about its colour and matching tokens by position does not work: you must match them by colour. Because every colour appears exactly once on every roster, and because every pip count from one to four appears on every roster, no colour, position, size, count or amount of ink singles out the answer. Exactly one colour is given the SAME pip count on all three rosters. Every other colour is given the same pip count on at most two of the three rosters, and each pair of rosters agrees on at least one further colour besides the answer, so reading only two rosters can never decide the answer: all three distant rosters must be compared. Which colour has the same pip count on all three rosters? Answer red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple.
